$comment: Figma <-> code parity. Each entry ties a Figma node to the CSS block that implements it
and, where one exists, its contract. evals/lint-parity.js validates the structure and
reports coverage; it cannot check Figma itself, so every entry records when a human or
an agent last confirmed it against the file.
This is deliberately NOT Code Connect. See system/components/README.md for why: real
Code Connect needs a Node toolchain and a publish step in CI, which ends this repo's
no-build-step property. This file gets detectable drift without that, and is the
input if Code Connect is adopted later.
Coverage is partial on purpose. Entries are added only when the node has actually been
read from Figma -- a guessed mapping is worse than none, because it looks authoritative.

global-navigation.role: Navigation chrome and the panel. Primary source for prototypes/navigation/.

openQuestions.issue: These have contracts but no parity entry. The Global Navigation file exposes one page (Menopause Footer), and the nav frames in it — Menu 6371:110, Search 6371:115, AI 6371:117, Alerts 6371:119 — sit inside frame 6371:107, which is hidden=true. That is a reference copy, not the canonical nav.
openQuestions.why_not_recorded: Anchoring a contract to a hidden copy would look authoritative while pointing at the wrong thing. Recorded as a gap instead; evals/lint-parity.js reports it every run.
openQuestions.needs: The canonical top-nav frame, or confirmation that the hidden Navigation frame is the source.

openQuestions.issue: The hidden nav copy draws the AI control at 36x36 with a 22x22 stars vector. main.css builds .ai-btn at 44px tall with .ai-btn__stars at 22x22 — the glyph matches, the control does not.
openQuestions.why_not_recorded: RESOLVED: 44px is correct and deliberate — the accessibility minimum for a touch target, as the contract's rationale states. The 36x36 in the hidden nav copy is not the current design. Figma frames will be refreshed later to match.

openQuestions.issue: 7417:3673 and 7417:3712 were both named "Access" and differed only by button label.

Worth noting the original assessment overstated it — the sections always disambiguated them in the layers tree; the frame names were ambiguous only in isolation.
